text: The Port Lands Flood Protection and Enabling Infrastructure Project ("The Project") is a comprehensive project for flood protecting southeastern portions of downtown Toronto. Waterfront Toronto requires access to approximately 160 acres of land owned by TPLC for short-term construction. This project will require permanently terminating some current leased tenancies and potential for short-term licenses, negatively impacting the revenue of TPLC over the life of the Project. TPLC's business revenues will experience a year over year loss as a result of the Project, during construction and, over the long term, as a result of the creation of the new river mouth and associated parks and infrastructure. Approved February 2018 as part of the City's 2018 Capital and Operating Budgets submission ( EX31.2w ), City staff were directed to execute a Contribution Agreement with the Federal and…

The Board of Directors of CreateTO: 1. Directed the Transition Lead, CreateTO to consult with the City of Toronto's Chief Financial Officer to review the implications of the revenue loss resulting from Port Lands Flood Protection project and to develop a plan that would support the financial sustainability of CreateTO and Toronto Port Lands Corporation, and report back to the CreateTO Board as part of the 2019 budget process.
